findings.issue: Fig 5 (main text, R1 Q2) omits the confound EXPERIMENTS.md §3.3 explicitly flags, and the computed framing states the collapse causally. Recomputed from experiment_results/rebuttal_fig5_cifar_paramfrac_scan/*.jsonl: all 15 runs share ONE configuration — k=64, lr=1.0, rtol=1e-3, loss=label_regression — with no per-fraction re-tuning. EXPERIMENTS.md line 356-358 says of exactly this scan: "this set point is the pre-Gram classic best and is still flagged SET POINT, STILL TENTATIVE ... It was NOT re-derived from the BN-fixed headline scan before launch, whose Sven optimum is k = 128, lr = 0.5, rtol = 1e-3", and line 350 attributes both blow-ups to "the scan's single lr = 1.0". My own recount of the headline label-reg scan confirms the confound: ALL 5 Sven divergences there are at lr=1.0 (k=64: 3/5 seeds, k=128: 2/5), and the Fig-5 f=1 runs (val 0.450/0.700/0.854, mean 0.668 ± 0.204) are the same volatile cell as the main scan's k=64/lr=1.0/rtol=1e-3 (0.46-0.95), versus the selected config's 0.4803 ± 0.013. Cell 27 nonetheless prints "At f <= 0.25 the run does not train at all ... with 2 diverged run(s)", attributing to f a collapse that a fixed, untuned, divergence-prone lr can produce on its own. Neither the Fig-5 markdown (cell 22) nor the facts print (cell 23, which prints k/lr/B/epochs/capture but not `loss`) nor the framing says the lr was never re-tuned per fraction or that this is not the headline-selected configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: In cell 22/27 add a computed line: print the single (k, lr, rtol) actually run, state that it is the pre-Gram tentative set point rather than the headline optimum (k=128, lr=0.5), that lr was NOT re-tuned per fraction, and that the two blow-ups are at the scan's only lr=1.0 — so the low-f collapse bounds "this config at this lr", not "masking at fraction f". Cite EXPERIMENTS.md §3.3.

findings.issue: Cell 0 (header markdown) claims "29 runs, ~122 GPU-h — a third of the campaign's GPU-hours in 0.1% of its runs". Recomputed by summing losses.total_time over every .jsonl in experiment_results/ (full census, 24,846 records): the 29 GPT-2 runs are 124.2 GPU-h of 1,539.5 GPU-h total = 8.1%, not a third — wrong by ~4x. mnist_scan_ce alone is 325.7 GPU-h and mnist_scan_labelRegression 229.8 GPU-h, either of which exceeds the GPT-2 total. The paired claim "0.1% of its runs" is correct (29/24,846 = 0.12%), and the header figure itself is slightly low (124.2, not ~122). Hard-coded in prose, so it will not self-correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the GPU-hour share sentence or compute it: the notebook already loads only its own scan, so quote "124 GPU-h for 29 runs (~4.3 GPU-h per run, the most expensive runs in the campaign)" and leave the campaign-share claim out unless it is computed from the root.

findings.issue: Section-2 markdown (cell 8) states "Both panels draw the same runs the tables above report — the selected configuration in {scan}_confirm ... so a curve cannot drift away from its table". Cell 10 (the vs-time panels) draws RUNS_TIME = selected_runs_by_method(scan,'timing'), and the timing pass uses the TUNING seeds, not the confirmation seeds: recomputed model_seed sets are {4000..4004} in cifar10_resnet_ce_scan_timing vs {4100..4104} in _confirm. The two panels therefore describe different runs, and the numbers differ: timing-pass Sven mean final val = 1.3995, confirmation = 1.4239 (the table's headline), tuning scan = 1.4028. Neither the figure title ("standalone timing pass, synchronised training time") nor the legend ("(5 seeds)") says which seeds. Same wording in nanogpt_analysis cell 6 (timing seeds 5000-5004 vs confirm 5100-5104). Aside: the task asks for val/test loss AND accuracy vs synchronised time; cell 10 draws only 'val' and 'test_acc' (no test loss, no val accuracy).
findings.suggested_fix: Reword cell 8 so the claim is scoped to the per-epoch panels, and label the time-axis figure as the standalone pass on the TUNING seeds (print the seed set, or have plot_curves put n_seeds and the seed range in the legend). Same one-line fix in nanogpt_analysis cell 6.

findings.issue: plot_sven_landscape marks a cell as provisional from `eligible`, not from `finished < attempted`, so a 3-of-5-seed cell is drawn exactly like a complete 5-seed one — which is the case that actually occurs. The docstring promises the opposite ("showing it unmarked would let a 2-seed mean be read as a 5-seed one") and cifar_analysis cell 15 tells the reader "cells that exist but have not finished more than half their seeds are drawn dashed and marked * — on the cross-entropy scan those are extension cells still landing". Recomputed on cifar10_resnet_ce_scan: the rtol extension is 9 cells, EVERY one of them partial (3 of 5 seeds now, 2-3 at execution), yet only 2 carry `*` in plots_v2/cifar/cifar10_resnet_ce_scan_sven_landscape.png; the other 7 (1.52, 1.40, 1.44, 1.36, 1.44, 1.39, 1.72) are unmarked. The unmarked 3-seed cell at lr=0.1/rtol=0.1 reads 1.36 and beats the red-ringed selection of record (1.40) — exactly the comparison a reader will draw off the figure. tests/test_large_figs.py::test_landscape_draws_the_provisional_cell only fixtures a 1-of-3 (ineligible) cell, so the real case is untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Set prov from `finished < attempted` (or annotate the seed count in the cell, e.g. "1.36 (3/5)") and keep `eligible` for the dashed edge; add a fixture cell with 3 of 5 seeds to the test.

findings.issue: The CIFAR-CE robustness bullet in the computed framing (cell 27) prints "Sven diverged on 0 of 195 runs of its own grid here" using GRID['attempted'].sum(). 195 = 175 records + 20 runs that have never started: recomputed, cifar10_resnet_ce_scan holds 177 Sven records today (175 at execution) and 0 are diverged under the wide rule, while cell 16 of the same notebook prints "20 run(s) of this grid have no record yet". The denominator therefore counts 20 non-existent runs as clean, inflating the robustness claim by ~11%, and it will keep moving as the extension lands. EXPERIMENTS.md §7 quotes the CIFAR-CE divergence row on its on-grid records ("740 on-grid runs") for exactly this reason. The label-regression bullet ("5 of 90") is correct — that grid has no missing runs, and I confirmed the 5 are k=64/lr=1.0/rtol=1e-4 (3) and k=128/lr=1.0/rtol=1e-4 (2).
findings.suggested_fix: Use finished + n_diverged + n_failed (records that exist) as the denominator, and print n_missing beside it: "0 of 175 runs recorded (20 of the 195 intended not yet started)".

findings.issue: Cell 18 markdown asserts "the tuning-budget table finds every Sven grid point on CIFAR a distinct trajectory: no two grid points collapse onto the same run", and cell 21 then prints CIFAR-CE Sven grid_points 39, distinct 35, distinct_frac 0.8974 — the notebook contradicts its own output three cells later (label-reg is 18/18 = 1.00, so only the CE row moved). Worse, the printed 0.897 is itself an artefact, not a collapse: I checked every pair of Sven configurations on every seed for a bit-identical losses.val curve and found NONE, so no two grid points share a trajectory. budget.trajectory_table computes distinct = mean over (seed, lr) groups x n_lr, which is diluted by the ragged extension (9 cells that exist for only 3 of 5 seeds and 3 of 5 lrs); the number will return toward 1.00 when the extension completes. Left as is, the notebook both states a falsehood about its own table and passes a ragged-grid artefact through as a tuning-budget fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Either recompute the claim from the printed table (and say "all but the ragged extension cells") or add one line noting that CIFAR-CE's distinct_frac < 1 is a ragged-grid artefact of trajectory_table's (seed, lr) grouping while the extension is partial, with the raw check that no two Sven trajectories coincide. Do not change budget.py (frozen).

findings.issue: plot_paramfrac_cost overlays the profile_results_v2 param_fraction study on the same axes and units as the records, and for the step-time panel the two say OPPOSITE things with nothing on the figure to say so. Recomputed from profile_helpers.load_profiles(): v2 gives masked 530.5/534.2/571.0/626.2 ms at f=0.05..0.5 and unmasked 845.7 ms at f=1 — masking looks 1.4x FASTER; the records give masked 342.1..389.1 ms and unmasked 178.3 ms — masking is 1.9-2.2x SLOWER. plots_v2/cifar/fig5_paramfrac_cost.png shows the dashed profile curve rising to a single orange point at 846 ms directly above the record curve's dip to 178 ms, with only a legend entry ("profile, mask=..."). The empty_cache explanation exists only in cell 25's printed text, so the figure alone — which is the object that goes into the rebuttal — reverses Fig 5's cost conclusion. (The memory panel is fine: profile 11829/12121/12993/14447/22978 MB vs records 11816/12107/12979/14433/22965 MB, which is why the overlay is invisible there.)
findings.suggested_fix: Until v3 lands, either drop the v2 step-time overlay (keep the memory one) or draw it greyed with an on-axes annotation "profile v2: empty_cache on every step, not comparable"; gate it on profile_helpers.results_root() being v3.

findings.issue: Neither Fig-5 figure carries the run counts or the objective. EXPERIMENTS.md line 353-355 states the requirement directly: "a Fig-5 point at pf <= 0.1 therefore rests on 2 surviving seeds of 3, which any seed band on that figure must show as finished / attempted". plots_v2/cifar/fig5_paramfrac_quality.png draws the f=0.05 and f=0.1 points as ordinary error bars with no marker of the reduced n (recomputed: 2 of 3 finished at both, 1 diverged each), the counts appearing only in the table printed below the figure. And in a notebook that reports two objectives side by side, no Fig-5 cell states which one this is: recomputed loss field = label_regression for all 15 runs, yet the section shows val 0.668 two cells after the CE table shows 1.424, inviting a direct comparison of a label-regression loss with a cross-entropy one.
findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the two left points with "2/3" (or open markers) in plot_paramfrac_quality, and put the objective plus the configuration in the Fig-5 titles/suptitle, computed from the frame (e.g. "CIFAR-10 / ResNet18, Sven, label regression, k=64, lr=1.0, rtol=1e-3, 3 seeds").

findings.issue: curve_axis double-prepends t=0 on a time axis for any key in large_figs.PRE_TRAINING_CURVES but not in scan_analysis.PRE_TRAINING_CURVES — i.e. 'train_eval_acc'. scan_analysis._has_pre_training already detects the pre-training entry by length (len(curve) == n_epochs + 1), so epoch_axis has ALREADY prepended the zero; the extra branch prepends a second one and the trailing truncation x[:len(curve)] then drops the last time. Reproduced on the real CIFAR-CE timing rows: curve_axis(..., 'val', 'time') -> [0, 62.879, 125.015, ...] ending 1244.38 (correct), while curve_axis(..., 'train_eval_acc', 'time') -> [0, 0, 62.879, 125.015, ...] ending 1182.24 — the whole curve is shifted one epoch late and its final point is plotted 62 s early. The branch is unreachable-useful for versus='epoch' (it recomputes the same arange) and wrong only for versus='time'. No figure in the three notebooks hits it today (train_eval_acc is drawn only vs epoch), so nothing published is wrong — but plot_curves accepts any key and the next cell that asks for it gets a silently mis-shifted axis.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the branch at lines 192-198 (epoch_axis's length check covers it), or guard it with `if not sa._has_pre_training(rows, curve, 'train')`. Add a test that curve_axis for 'train_eval_acc' vs 'time' equals curve_axis for 'val' vs 'time'.

findings.issue: The computed framing (cell 12) quotes "best baseline Muon at 3.741" without carrying over what its own cell-8 table found: Muon's and SOAP's optima are on the HIGH edge of their lr sweeps (Muon best lr 0.003 = max tried, SOAP the same; recomputed, both confirmed). The comparison is therefore conservative in Sven's favour — two baselines may not have been tuned out — and the gap the paper quotes (+39%) is a lower bound. The direction is safe, but the caveat is the mirror image of the k=B=16 caveat the framing does state, and it is one line away in the same notebook.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a computed clause to the framing bullet: name the methods whose best lr is at an edge of their sweep, so the +39% is stated as a lower bound.

findings.issue: The BatchNorm gate (cell 3) asserts bn_mode == 'batch' on the two tuning scans only (600 + 765 records), but every headline number in the notebook comes from _confirm, and the cost table from _timing, and the rank plot from _diag — none of which the gate covers. The header markdown states the policy as universal ("Every optimizer on both scans ran with bn_mode: batch"), which is why the assertion exists rather than a sentence. I verified the claim holds — all 6 result-dependent passes are {'batch': 55} each, 330 records — so this is scope, not a wrong number.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the loop over the four passes per scan (the freshness cell already enumerates them) so the assertion covers the records the tables are built from.

findings.issue: Cell 16's CIFAR-CE grid table is introduced as "the grid the selection was made on, as the scan itself sees it (eligible -> fewest diverged -> seed mean)", and the row marked selected=True is fourth, below three extension cells (1.354, 1.356, 1.390 vs the selection's 1.403). Nothing in that cell says why: the scan's own current ordering has diverged from the frozen selection of record (bench/best_configs.json, generated_at 2026-09-20T03:58, pre-extension). Only the PROVISIONAL banner 13 cells earlier covers it, and a reader who lands on the table sees what looks like a selection-rule violation.
findings.suggested_fix: One computed line under the table: if the top eligible row is not the selected row, print "the scan's current best (<cfg>, <n> seeds) is not the selection of record (generated_at ...) — see the PROVISIONAL banner; re-run tools/select_best.py".
